title: Microled Cost Orchard — export-first token-cost view & pricing pattern library
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Product and finance teams need a reliable, auditable way to slice token-level cost down to business artifacts (route, model variant, workspace) and export that view for reconciliation and contracts. Existing console panels surface some cost rollups but are not export-first, force heavy UI navigation, and lack role-aware column presets or a simulated pricing layer for forecasting.

Goal: Deliver a prototype UI/interaction pattern for an export-first Token Cost View that: 1) lets users define attribution keys and aggregation windows, 2) previews the derived rate-card mapping (per-token, per-invocation, per-embedding) inline, 3) supports CSV / Parquet / JSONL export schemas with role-aware templates, and 4) includes a pricing-patterns panel (presets, simulator) that non-engineering stakeholders can use to run reconciliation scenarios.

Scope: Console UX + prototype (Figma) + design spec for engineering handoff. Out of scope: backend ETL implementation and billing system integration (ENG tickets will handle that).

Key concepts proposed: 
- Export-first flow: primary CTA is Export; preview table is first-class and lightweight.
- Attribution composer: drag-to-add keys (route, model, variant, region, customer_tag) and choose aggregation (minute/hour/day) with live cost preview.
- Rate-card overlay: shows which rate profile will be used for each column (hosted vs dedicated) and highlights fallback mappings when model variant not mapped.
- Role-aware templates: admin, finance, SRE presets that control visible columns, absolute vs per-unit modes, and include/hide sensitive IDs.
- Pricing patterns panel: quick-presets (developer/dev-only discounts, enterprise-commit tiers, metered), slider to adjust per-token rates for simulation, and a compare mode to show delta vs current billing.
- Export schema options: column definitions for CSV/Parquet/JSONL, field-level anonymization toggle, timestamp timezone normalization, and a manifest file for large exports.

decision_log: 2025-02-15: Chose export-first over dashboard-first after PM/finance workshop — export is primary use-case for reconciliation.
2025-02-17: Settled on three role templates (Admin, Finance, SRE) and one custom template mode — reduces complexity for MVP.
2025-02-19: Decided to surface rate-card overlay rather than inline editable prices to avoid accidental billing edits in console.
2025-02-21: Agreed to support CSV and Parquet for MVP; JSONL deferred for larger batch exports after usage telemetry.
2025-02-22: Opted for a client-side simulation slider with server-side check before export to ensure parity with billing rates.
comments: PM Feedback (Arjun Rao, 2025-02-16): Need clearer tie-in to Dedicated vs Hosted capacity; include an explicit indicator when data is from Dedicated pools so finance knows contractual boundaries.

Engineering Review (Sofia Martinez, 2025-02-18): Backend needs a manifest endpoint that describes column schema; will implement ENG-1982. Also flagged potential performance issue for minute-level aggregation on large workspaces.
Design Review (Kara Nguyen, 2025-02-19): Table density is high—propose condensed row mode and compact headers to fit more columns for finance exports.
Security (Ben Alonzo, 2025-02-20): Add field-level anonymization toggle for PII (customer_id) and audit log entry for every export. Marked for a follow-up security microtask.
Finance (Lena Fischer, 2025-02-21): Include an 'explain' column that maps each cost row to the rate component (base, burst, quantization discount) to speed reconciliations.
Product (Victor Lim, 2025-02-22): Recommend adding a 'what-if' save slot for pricing simulations so users can share scenarios with stakeholders.
tradeoffs_considered: Dense table vs readable table: chose dense default with toggle to readable to balance finance needs and general usability.
Client-side simulation vs server-side: client simulation is faster for UX but requires server validation before export to maintain billing accuracy.
Expose raw token-level IDs vs anonymize: provide role-aware templates and a per-field anonymization switch rather than hiding entirely.
Export formats: CSV/Parquet for MVP (wider tooling support); JSONL will be added for streaming consumers once telemetry justifies it.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype: Figma prototype demonstrates attribution composer, rate-card overlay, and export workflow end-to-end.
Design spec: Component-level spec (table, templates, pricing-patterns UI) with accessibility notes and responsive behavior.
Engineering handoff: JSON manifest spec attached to ENG-1982 and PR #5123 created for frontend implementation.
Usability review: 3 stakeholder sessions (Finance, SRE, Admin) with at least 2 actionable improvements captured and addressed.
Telemetry hookpoints: list of events (export_start/export_complete/preview_rate_card_open) documented for instrumentation.

notes_for_engineering: Frontend should request manifest endpoint (ENG-1982) before enabling exports; use preview API to calculate estimated export size.
Support server-side validation step for pricing simulation exports to ensure exported numbers match billing system rates.
Provide compact table mode and column-visibility presets that map to role templates; persist templates per workspace.
Include export manifest with column datatypes, example rows, and timezone normalization metadata.
